The hidden labels Experience Bias and Attribution Bias are benchmark target labels, so equivalence was adjudicated by mechanism and the supplied hidden definitions.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Panel 5 looked similar on the face of it, so when the contractor asked whether to reuse that pattern or commission something new, I specified the Panel 3 pattern. There was exploration data showing different joint orientation in Panel 5 and a fault splay that Panel 3 didn't have, but the overall rock looked like the same family to me.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant transfers a personally successful Panel 3 support design to Panel 5 based on surface similarity while discounting case-specific exploration evidence.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: He was under an unsupported section of back when it came down, and that's a positioning call he makes every shift. That's the part of the incident that was directly within his control, so that's where I put the emphasis in the report. It was noted, but the more immediate explanation was where the loader was actually sitting at the time. That's the piece that was in front of me and easiest to point to.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant foregrounds the operator's behavior and downweights the available elevated-joint-density ground-condition explanation when attributing the fall of ground.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Honestly, that's just how we've always operated. A single seismic event with convergence a bit above average isn't unusual for that ground — we get blips like that periodically and the standard approach has always been to keep the cycle running unless something more definitive shows up. Stopping the schedule every time there's a minor signal would grind the whole panel transition to a halt, and that's not how we do things here.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant justifies continuing the pre-existing schedule primarily by established practice and normal operating procedure despite new seismic and convergence information.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: It's a specific number, calculated from our stability model, and it cleared our standard threshold. That gave me something concrete to point to when the manager needed an answer. As for the spalling reports, minor spalling happens periodically in that ground and doesn't usually change the overall picture. On top of that, I've managed plenty of ground issues before — if something came up post-blast, I was confident we could respond and adjust support on the fly. That's part of why I felt comfortable saying go rather than waiting out the review.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant treats the 1.42 model output as a concrete sufficient basis despite mismatched calibration and spalling, and separately relies on confidence in personal ability to manage future ground issues.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: Decision point 1: whether to continue the existing Panel 5 firing schedule after the seismic and convergence warning.
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: Defaulting to the pre-existing firing schedule despite new seismic/convergence data, treating continuation as requiring less justification than change.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: The RAG label exactly matches the hidden target label.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: The finding identifies continuation of the established schedule as the default response to new monitoring information and ties it to the schedule decision.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: Valid participant quotations directly support the established-procedure rationale.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: Decision point 2: whether to reuse the Panel 3 support pattern or commission a new Panel 5 design.
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: Generalizing a personally successful past support design from a superficially similar panel without adequately weighing case-specific exploration data.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: Representativeness heuristic is a related similarity-based construct, but it is not an approved equivalent of the benchmark's Experience Bias label under the supplied ontology-free matching rule.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: The mechanism fully captures transfer of a personally successful prior design from a similar-looking panel while discounting different joint orientation and the fault splay; the label differs.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: Multiple valid participant quotations accurately support the similarity and prior-success reasoning.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: Decision point 3: causal attribution of the Panel 5 fall-of-ground incident.
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: Favoring a dispositional/behavioral causal explanation (operator error) over an available situational explanation (flagged ground conditions).
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: Fundamental attribution error is an established scholarly formulation of the person-versus-situation attribution distortion specified by Attribution Bias here.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: The finding fully captures emphasis on the operator's controllable positioning while downweighting the flagged joint-density and unsupported-back conditions.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: Valid quotations accurately preserve the participant's causal attribution and acknowledgment of competing situational evidence.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: Decision point 4: whether the 1.42 stability-model result justified firing before the full geotechnical review.
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: Treating a precise numerical model output as a reliable basis for judgment despite mismatched calibration source and conflicting field evidence.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: No identified occurrence fully claims this hidden instance. The anchoring candidate is not promoted because its evidence is explicitly tentative and its mechanism is incomplete.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: The candidate notices the concrete model number and known limitations, but does not establish that the participant treated the model as valid or reliable despite the conflicting field evidence.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: The RAG output contains the relevant model and spalling facts, but no qualifying identified finding for this hidden instance.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: Decision point 4: personal confidence in managing uncertain post-blast ground issues.
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: Expressing high confidence in personal capability to manage uncertain future ground issues, independent of the model output itself.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: Overconfidence effect is an established equivalent formulation of the supplied Overconfidence Bias target.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: The finding separately identifies confidence in personal capability and prior track record as a reason to accept uncertain future ground risk, distinct from reliance on the model output.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: Valid participant quotations directly support the self-assessed capability mechanism and its role in approving firing.

unmatched_rag_predictions.why_not_an_exact_strict_match: obs_004 already supplies the one-to-one exact Status quo bias match for cb_01. obs_001 overlaps the same schedule-continuation episode but emphasizes normalizing the warning rather than the hidden default-to-status-quo mechanism, so it is an extra duplicate claim rather than a second occurrence.

The candidate is based on a valid quotation and identifies possible anchoring on 1.42, but it expressly leaves open ordinary professional practice and does not establish the full illusion-of-validity mechanism of treating a mismatched model as reliable despite conflicting field evidence.

candidates.details: The candidate is a useful, evidence-grounded possibility but lacks sufficient evidence for a full mechanism match and does not use the hidden target label or an approved equivalent. It therefore adds a fourth-threshold false positive without rescuing cb_04.

high_only.detection_interpretation: All four eligible positive segments contain at least one high-confidence identified finding; no eligible negative segments were supplied.

high_and_moderate.detection_interpretation: The cumulative threshold is unchanged because every identified occurrence is high confidence; all four positive segments are detected.

corpus_support_audit.assessment_note: The RAG explicitly states that no retrieved corpus passages were supplied and provides no citation metadata. Corpus support therefore does not affect the primary scores.

confidence_tradeoff.increment_from_all_confidence_to_all_con: Segment metrics remain unchanged; strict instance precision falls from 0.6000 to 0.5000 and F1 from 0.6000 to 0.5455, while mechanism-first precision falls from 0.8000 to 0.6667 and F1 from 0.8000 to 0.7273 because the anchoring candidate is an additional false positive.

overall_evaluation_summary.segment_level_primary_result: All 4 of 4 positive reasoning segments were detected at every threshold; there were no negative eligible segments for false-alarm testing.
overall_evaluation_summary.strict_label_plus_mechanism_result: 3 of 5 hidden instances were strict matches at the first three thresholds (precision 0.6000, recall 0.6000, F1 0.6000). The fourth-threshold candidate adds a false positive.
overall_evaluation_summary.mechanism_first_result: 4 of 5 hidden instances matched by mechanism at the first three thresholds (precision 0.8000, recall 0.8000, F1 0.8000). The Experience Bias mechanism was recovered under the near-neighbor Representativeness heuristic label; the Illusion of validity instance was missed.
overall_evaluation_summary.candidate_tier_value_assessment: The single candidate is a useful, grounded near miss localized to the correct final-approval segment, but it is insufficiently evidenced for a true positive and lowers fourth-threshold precision.
main_failure_modes: The RAG did not identify the hidden Illusion of validity instance.
It used a near-neighbor label for Experience Bias, preventing a strict match despite full mechanism recovery.
It produced a duplicate Normalcy bias claim for the status-quo segment.
The candidate Anchoring effect was not sufficiently supported and became a fourth-threshold false positive.
main_strengths: All positive reasoning segments were localized correctly at the segment level.
Fundamental attribution error and Overconfidence effect were approved equivalents with full mechanism matches.
The Experience Bias mechanism was captured in detail despite the label mismatch.
Quoted interview evidence was valid and faithful, with no fabricated quotations or citation inconsistencies.
overall_evaluation_summary.benchmark_interpretation: This run has perfect segment-level sensitivity on the supplied positive-only map, but instance-level performance depends strongly on ontology treatment: strict F1 is 0.6000 versus mechanism-first F1 of 0.8000 before candidate inclusion. Candidate inclusion adds no recovered instance and reduces precision.
